question.prompt: Given the larger of two circles with center \(P\) and radius \(p\) and the smaller with center \(Q\) and radius \(q.\) Draw \(\overline{PQ}.\) Which of the following statements is false?

solutions.explanation:
Each statement says “can,” so we may use a different placement of the circles for each statement. Let \(d=PQ\). Since one circle is larger, \(p>q>0\).

For A, place the smaller circle inside the larger one so that they touch internally. Then \(d=p-q\).

For B, let the circles touch externally. Then \(d=p+q\).

For C, separate the circles by a gap. Then \(d>p+q\).

For D, external tangency also works: \(d=p+q>p-q\), because \(q>0\).

Thus A through D are all possible. None of these statements is false, so the answer is \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Check possible circle positions
